name: Homeschool Compass
promise: Clear, honest guides for families teaching at home — what each curriculum actually teaches, what your state actually requires, and who each option is not for. Every claim links to its source.
editorialPolicyHtml:
Homeschool Compass exists because most homeschool advice comes from people selling something — a curriculum, a course, a co-op membership. We sell none of those, so we are free to tell you when an option is wrong for your family.

Our position on worldview

We tell you exactly what worldview a material carries. We do not tell you which worldview to hold. Homeschooling in the United States includes deeply religious families and firmly secular ones, and both deserve to know what is inside a book before they buy it. A parent who wants a Christian science course and a parent who wants mainstream science are asking the same practical question — what does this actually teach? — and we answer it the same way for both.

To keep that honest, we report two separate facts about every curriculum we cover, and we never merge them:

  • Content worldview — is there religious content in the material itself?
  • Publisher affiliation — is the company behind it religious?

These are different questions, and different families care about different ones. By reporting both, we never have to hand you our own verdict on a contested call — you get the two facts and decide for yourself. When a publisher makes no statement either way, we label it unstated, which is not the same as neutral.

How we source

Every worldview label quotes the publisher's own words, links to the page we took them from, and records the month we last checked. Every legal requirement comes from the state's own published rules. If we cannot find a claim at its source, we do not publish the claim — we would rather leave a gap than fill it with a guess.

We also state the limits of what we checked. Our labels reflect a publisher's stated position and the samples they make public; we do not claim to have read every page of every course, because we have not.

On authorship

This is an early build of Homeschool Compass, published under our editorial team rather than a personal byline. We compile and verify from primary sources instead of claiming credentials or classroom experience we do not have — and we show you where every fact came from so you can check it yourself. We do not write in the voice of a homeschooling parent we are not.

On money

We plan to earn through advertising and through affiliate links to some of the materials we cover. A commission never changes a ranking or a verdict. When our conclusion is "don't buy this," it stays "don't buy this" whether or not there is a commission attached.

On mistakes

Publishers revise their materials and states change their rules. When we get something wrong, we correct it, date the correction, and leave the record visible rather than quietly editing the page.
